label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
**One star for now: Promising software, but we need support that responds**

Our library moved its catalog and circulation to Stackhouse Cloud on October 19. The software looked good in the demo, and I still think the staff interface is better than our old system. The idea is not the problem. The support has been.

Bridger Bend Community Library has one branch, two full-time staff members, volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year contract in June for $14,200 a year. Since October 28, checkouts have worked only offline on one laptop, and our holds queue has been wiped out—about 640 holds gone.

Our support ticket has been open for 12 days. We have received three replies, each saying the issue has been escalated to engineering. Our sales representative promised a “dedicated migration specialist.” What we got was a shared inbox.

These are not abstract problems for a library our size. A retired rancher recently drove 40 minutes to pick up his held large-print Westerns. We had no record of his hold and had to send him home with nothing. One of our volunteers has been writing checkouts on index cards like it’s 1975.

Our county budget hearing is November 18, and this contract is on the agenda. I need more than another escalation notice before then. I am asking Stackhouse to have a **named person call me this week**, explain what is being done to restore circulation and the holds queue, and give us a realistic timeline.

For other small-library directors considering Stackhouse: ask for support response times in writing before you sign. Ask who will handle your migration, and what happens when a serious problem cannot be resolved promptly.

I’m giving one star for now. If Stackhouse fixes these problems and provides the support we were promised, I’ll revisit this review.
